reconstruction_notes.en: Original7m-wide representative shore-platform patch: a broad low gently seaward-sloping abrasion bench remains continuous with a retreated rear cliff face, with restrained shallow weathered pans and one joint. Clear cropped bedrock sides and back, no high waterfall stair, tiny isolated stone or sea-stack substitution. NPS coastal context and primary GSA shore-platform/cliff study consulted. Weathering and erosion contributions vary; not a claim that waves alone universally cut platforms. Nominal dimensions, local slope, palette and layout are art choices, not a mapped ancient site, exact tide level or fluid simulation.

assets.author: Leon Made This / s010s

description.en: Evidence-informed WHOLE adult Wiwaxia corrugata exterior reconstruction, nominal50mm long not a measured specimen replica. Smith2014 documents eight transverse rows and anterior organization; Zhang/Smith/Shu2015 explicitly reinterprets anterior organization in W.corrugata as ninth serial row, based also on adult ROM57707. Model uses eight trunk rows PLUS anterior paired fan; it does not falsely assert both authors use identical counting or impose juvenile W.papilio proportions/spine absence.2015 correction2023 adds omitted dataset only, not retraction. Molluscan versus deeper lophotrochozoan affinity remains uncertain. Colors, exact posture, body depth and soft margins inferred. Fine rib count simplified; no internal gut simulation, fossil scan or copied mesh.
description.zh: Wiwaxia 完整个体外形研究，不是精确标本复制。躯干部八排加前端成对扇状骨片的表达保留文献计数差异，不把不同研究解释混为定论。

description.en: Evidence-informed incomplete phragmocone fragment, Spyroceras melolineatum holotype UMUT PM18493. Rear and closed mineral fracture faces inferred. name.zh: Phragmoceras · SM75 缺损正模壳标本

description.en: Evidence-informed stylized depiction of the damaged SM 75 holotype. Missing apex and incomplete hyponomic margin retained. Aperture depth, hidden surfaces and limestone palette are original conservative interpretations, not measured restoration. Historical 43/33 mm measurements have undefined axes; this model is not a direct calibrated restoration of those measurements. Neither a complete deep hyponomic tube nor a living animal is reconstructed.
description.zh: 依原文制作的 SM 75 缺损壳标本风格化表现；不补顶端及完整漏斗口。口腔深度、隐藏面及色彩属于明确标注的保守推定。 文献中的43/33毫米量值轴向未明，模型尺寸不等同于这些量值的直接复原。 不复原完整深漏斗管或活体动物。

assets.scientific_scope_departure: Original provisional curved inflated shell with strongly constricted slit-like aperture target is narrowed to damaged SM75. A complete apex, deep complete hyponomic tube and entire terminal aperture are not restored. Preserved U and damage margins are stylized, not source-measured contours.

reference_credits.title: Manda (2007), New Silurian nautiloids Phragmoceras and Tubiferoceras from the Prague Basin
reference_credits.use: consulted-only; no reference media, mesh or texture incorporated

diagnostic_targets: Broad low heavy oval feathered trunk, no visible or vestigial wings.
Exceptionally short stout tarsometatarsi and broad feet, unlike long slender ostrich legs.
Long thick forward-curving neck, small rounded head and sturdy pointed decurved bill; no casque or giant duck bill.
Three forward clawed toes plus small hind toe per foot, no ostrich two-toed feet or webbing.
Restrained shaggy feather contour, scaly bare lower legs, no fan tail.
Thighs covered by bulky body, readable negative spaces between stout legs and toes.
uncertainties: Living soft contour, posture and precise plumage pattern/colors are inferred; feather evidence permits variation, not a fixed proven painted pattern.
AM LB5950 is mounted museum skeleton; mount pose and missing ribs do not define exact living silhouette.
No claim that limb measurements, separate tarsometatarsus and skeleton photo are same individual.
Tring photo caption says heavy-footed but filename says eastern-moa; it is excluded from production reference set to avoid ambiguous identity.

frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Entire Silurian animal anchored to serial-ground holotype OUMNH C.29640; no fossil slab or borrowed published mesh.

scale.note: 23.2mm and 9.2mm directly published same specimen. Other lengths are conservative modeling partitions estimated from same-specimen images; adjust to total, not independent measurements. Vaulted height inferred ~4mm; no foreign specimen scale.

anatomy: Semioval smooth vaulted shield; eyes not evidenced. Eleven free rear tergites: reduced concealed first, eight preabdominal and three postabdominal segments overall; tapering telson with two short terminal points.

Seven prosomal appendage pairs: elongated flexible chelicerae with tiny terminal chela; limbs2-5 each have separately inserting inner and outer rami; limb6 inner ramus only, nonchelate terminal; limb7 small spine-fringed flap.
Inner rami2-5 six podomeres plus terminal claw; outer rami shorter, five podomeres with terminal spine brushes. Six paired lamellate gill groups under preabdomen; attachment uncertain.
restoration_boundaries: Images are serial-grinding digital fossil reconstructions, not unprocessed photographs or artistic concept evidence. Distinct color segmentation in atlas is not biological coloration.
No copying research meshes/STL; construct original low-poly geometry from cited morphology. No new eyes, giant genal horns, fused modern horseshoe rear shield or scorpion sting.
Restore neutral symmetric stance instead of preserving taphonomic crossed/asymmetric limbs; exact minor joint angles, lamella count simplification, thickness and muted color are artistic choices.
Atlas figure3 A/B only match holotype; C/D/E other animals excluded.

scope_correction.original: compact nothosaur body with shorter neck and paddlelike forefeet
scope_correction.evidence_update: Renesto,Ragni and Magnani2025 demonstrate actual webbed manus and pes with separately visible digit tips, explicitly not a continuous flipper outline. Retain robust oar-like forelimb and compact torso, but correct old paddlelike forefoot wording to webbed clawless hands. Neck is elongate but shorter than trunk, not a neckless animal or a plesiosaur swan-neck.
scope_correction.authorization: Root00:39 confirmed genus-level target has no species hardconstraint and accepted evidence-based webbed-foot correction without changing whole-organism scope. No invented smooth flipper to satisfy outdated wording.
scope_correction.species_choice: Earlier L.balsami candidate replaced by same-genus L.valceresii because MCSN8713 has direct skin and dimensional evidence. Balsami photos/PDF retained only as research trail, not geometry/soft-tissue source.

evidence_anchors.primary: Renesto et al.2025 doi10.1186/s13358-025-00396-z. MCSN8713 virtually complete skeleton with carbonized skin, lateLadinian upperKalkschieferzone, MerideLimestone, ValMara MonteSanGiorgio Switzerland.
evidence_anchors.actual_images: Fig3A whole actual dorsal fossil with100mmbar; Fig4A skull10mmbar; Fig9A/B actual hand/forelimb10mmbar; Fig10actual foot5mmbar; Fig11A/C actual limb skin vsB/D interpreted silhouettes.
evidence_anchors.not_actual_fossils: Fig3B is third-party scientific3D reconstruction; Fig13 is third-party reconstruction with generative-fill background. Neither is a true referencephoto or model to copy. Do not download/copy their mesh or recreate image as publictexture.
evidence_anchors.taxonomy: 2025 author assignment explicitly L.valceresii with confidence; genus diagnoses and some nothosaur phylogenetic relationships remain debated. This is not Ceresiosaurus or a new generic transfer.
evidence_anchors.preservation: Skull fractured and partly missing snout; terminal30caudals fault-displaced75cm but remained articulated. Do not include fracture or75cm offset in animal. Skin widened by flattening especially limbs; exact thickness inferred.

scale.basis: Renesto2025 Table1 MCSN8713 column only:820mm total,75.5skull,13.3nariswidth,29orbitwidth,56humerus,55.7femur. Never use900/980mm other individuals. Neck/trunk/tail partition and flesh thickness are approximate inferred proportions, not listed caliper measurements.

morphology: Whole compact nothosaur: low triangular head, slight rostral constriction, slender moderate neck distinctly shorter than torso, broad low elongated torso, continuously tapering long tail. No plesiosaur-length neck or snake-thin body.

Exactly four limbs; forelimbs robust and oar-like overall, with broad fleshy upper arms and posterior axillary transition reaching some way down anterior trunk. Hindlimbs more gracile in bones but also fleshy; do not make four narrow dolphin flippers.

Both hands and feet are webbed with five separately visible short rounded digit tips at each outer margin. Web covers most digit length yet terminates with shallow interdigital notches. No claws, no isolated spidery fingers, no smooth closed oval paddle hiding all digits.

Use actual Fig9/10 detail to keep five tips credible without exaggerating fingerlength. Forelimb humerus and femur approximately equal56vs55.7mm; forelimb robustness is not achieved by doubling its length.

Thick forelimb-to-trunk tissue is inferred musculature supported by preserved skin; recover reasonable3D fullness rather than extruding flattened skin as a giant wing/fin. Distalweb thin with gradual transition to rounded proximal arm.

Head length75.5mm and orbit-level width29mm supported. External eyes are near anterolateral/dorsolateral skull, not posterior temporal openings. Temporal fenestrae are covered with living tissue, no exposed skull holes.

Closed or slightly open mouth, restrained slender forward-pointing anterior teeth if shown; not crocodile sawtooth rim or paired giant tusks. Broken snout restored conservatively to reported triangular outline.
Tail tapers in a continuous low axial shape, no dorsal fin, vertical caudal crescent, whale flukes or decorative sail. Modest lateral swimming curve permissible, no fault-offset geometry.

Skin scales are real: small juxtaposed subrectangular non-overlapping scales best evidenced on limbs, smaller toward extremities. Lowpoly simplify to subtle shallow surface segmentation or tonal facets, not armor spikes/large crocodile scutes. Exact wholebody pattern and colour unknown.
Neutral low swimming pose, neck approximately horizontal. No slab, groundstand, bones, specimen label or copied3D reconstruction.
uncertainty: Dorsal compressedfossil is not a true uncompressed3D scan; lateral bodydepth and headheight inferred.
Skin outline supports thick proximal limbs but flattening exaggerates breadth; do not treat all planar width as a membrane wing.
Scale preservation sparse over torso, inferred coverage from few retained scales not a known colourpattern.
No four-angle actualphoto set; four outputrenders inspect bounded3D reconstruction based on real complete dorsal fossil and detailphotos.
Original paddlelike terminology corrected with cited2025 actualwebbedfoot evidence. No species mixing into chosenMCSN8713.
frozen_scientific_scope.palette: Restrained grey/olive, subtle lighter underside as artistic convention; no claimed preserved colour.

frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Whole Silurian animal. Main outline/scale is Siveter2003 Fig4 virtual fossil, about7mm long; caption provides no accession. Same-species C.29557 used solely to clarify appendages, not covert scale substitution.

scale.uncertainty: 7mm is rounded caption length; component dimensions approximate same image proportions, not caliper measurements. Live posture and oblique image imply ~20percent proportional uncertainty.

anatomy: High arch/box-like cephalic shield with an open anterior gape. Reduced tapering rear body, free anterior tergites then compact fused posterior unit, narrow articulated tail spine. Not modern horseshoe outline.

Seven cephalic appendage pairs: slender long chelicerae; pairsII-V robust segmented brush-bearing exopods pointing forward/up and ventrally oriented endopods. Separate body-wall insertion for inner/outer branches per2012 revision, not forks on leg shafts.
PairVI locomotory inner branch with small outer tendril interpretation rather than a fifth large brush; pairVII short flap-like. Preserve small conservative terminals, not giant claws.

Use2013 revised dorsal counting: four anterior tergites (the fourth previously grouped posteriorly), three fused posterior segments, separate telson-base boss not counted as an eighth trunk segment. Six paired ventral opercula: first three more developed respiratory lamellae, last three reduced covers.
restoration_boundaries: Fig4 is a fossil-derived digital reconstruction, not an ordinary surface photo or color evidence. Build original geometry, never import published reconstruction mesh.
Unknown accession of Fig4 remains unknown; C.29557 in2025 Fig1C/2C-D is same-species anatomical comparator and visibly smaller, not the7mm measured individual.
Brush feeding function is hypothesis, not behavior proven by fossil; stance/color and minor missing fine bristles inferred. No invented compound eyes.
2025 figures contain modern shrimp and other genera: only Offacolus1C and2C-D informative here.

Slight gape makes caniniforms readable; keep canine scale relative skull, not saber-tooth-cat overgrowth.
Hand digits: three main curved clawed grasping digits with two small reduced lateral digits; palm faces inward not flat-down pronation.
Entire body retained with neck trunk two arms two hindlimbs and tapering tail. No armour plates.
uncertainties: Wholebody proportions combine specimens and anatomical reconstruction; AM4766 figure is incomplete posteriorly and does not directly show complete tail.
Skin colour softtissue and presence of filaments unknown for this taxon; restrained smooth lowpoly skin avoids claiming feather evidence.
Caniniform function and dietary nuance not inferred from tusks alone; no sex claim.
AM4766 and SAM-PK-K1332 remain distinct specimens; no transfer of scale between them as direct measurement.
frozen_scientific_scope.runtime_profile: Static opaque palette-only GLB, no textures, skins, animation, compression or extensions. Independent QA required; browser/GPU/populated-scene review remains separate.

diagnostic_targets: Broad robust feathered body, heavy walking legs and thick neck; no gracile ostrich body.
Tall but comparatively broad rounded goose-like upper bill, not a raptor hook or huge deep Dromornis block.
Low broad triangular casque across dorsal bill base, not a tall cassowary horn or Sylviornis exaggerated knob.
Two small reduced folded wings present, unlike completely wingless moa.
Three forward digits with blunt hoof-like claws, no recurved raptorial talons, no swimming webbing implied from goose nickname.
Conservative muted feather/skin palette, bare head-neck coverage and colors treated as inferred.
uncertainties: 2024 cranial reconstruction combines fossils with deformation corrections; do not copy fossil crushing or cracked edges into live anatomy.
Soft contour, skin coverage, plumage and colors not preserved, author art is interpretation.
Overall2m body height is an estimate; original limb specimen dimensions not measured here.
Exact relationship within Galloanserae unresolved; giant-goose popular shorthand not taxonomic identification as Anatidae.

evidence_anchors.postcranial: Rieppel1994 SMNS14733 measured associated postcranial bones; Fig36 explicit skeletal RECONSTRUCTION, not actual complete fossil. 2024 Cabezuelo-Hernandez et al same-genus comparison confirms32-34dorsals in GPIT-PV31566, incomplete neck/tail in both principal skeletons.
evidence_anchors.museum: Ghedoghedo2010 photo of Stuttgart mounted skeleton, real photograph but reconstructed/composite display, no readable accession. Do NOT claim this is complete original SMNS14733 or measure total from perspectival photograph.
evidence_anchors.taxonomic_boundary: S.gaillardoti valid2024 Simosauridae; Paludidraco is separate filter-feeding genus, NOT geometry source. Rieppel1994 treats guilielmi synonym; original holotype gaillardoti lost.
evidence_anchors.incomplete_parts: Tail/neck counts, distal phalangeal formula, soft tissue and pigmentation are uncertain; reconstruct conservatively from same-genus Fig36 and mounted layout, not invent fossil preservation.

scale.basis: Gregory S.Paul Princeton Field Guide size table lists S.gaillardoti SMNS14733 4.2m/200kg/2.7density. Total is an author reconstruction ESTIMATE, not an intact specimen measurement;1994 diagnosis gives general3-4m range. Use4.2m as approximate representative normalization, not verified caliper length.
scale.interpretation: All body partitions/flesh dimensions above are approximate visual reconstruction ratios from Fig36 and museum mount, NOT table measurements. Fig8 skull belongs another individual; use shape ratios only, not its size as SMNS14733 skull.

morphology: Whole animal, low broad bluntly rounded triangular head, no needle snout or bulbous frog head. No constricted rostrum. Eyes dorsolateral anterior to large posterior cheek region; cover all bony fenestrae with flesh.
Moderately elongate neck distinctly narrower than torso, shorter than torso and smoothly blended. Broad ribcage, robust elongated trunk. No giant plesiosaur swan neck.

Exactly four short robust limbs. Forelimbs stronger and longer than hindlimbs, humerus/femur ratio1.28 supports distinction. Bent upper/lower limb sections lead into five-digit swimming hands/feet. Do not turn entire limbs into dolphin paddles.

Five digits per limb; degree of webbing, distal digit lengths and small terminal claws are uncertain. Use conservative partly webbed broad hands/feet with five short visible tips, no exaggerated talons or invented hyperphalangy. Not direct skin evidence.

Continuous long tapering tail with no imposed fluke, dorsal fin, crest, plates or spines. Neck/tail exact lengths are inferred, not claimed preserved. Gentle near-horizontal swimming pose, no rigid extreme neck bend.
Slight jaw opening to show a few short stout broad blunt crowns, not needle fangs, large tusks or flat placodont paving teeth. Tooth number is visual simplification, not counted complete dentition.
Neutral muted grey-brown dorsal and lighter ventral colors are artistic inference, no bold unsupported markings. No exposed skeleton, mount supports, slab, labels or props.
must_not: No Paludidraco anatomy or filter comb; no Nothosaurus needle fangs/waisted rostrum.
No scientific claim of direct soft-tissue preservation or complete original mounted specimen.
Do not reproduce fossil breaks, fenestra holes, missing skull bones or museum armatures.

anatomy: Broad rounded anterior shield with thin edge, vaulted rather than flat modern horseshoe rim. Subtle ophthalmic/cardial relief; eye evidence uncertain, no conspicuous invented compound eyes.

Ten free opisthosomal segments with blunt extended lateral points and modest axial/pleural nodes; rear three near-equal width form less distinct postabdomen. Needle-like tapering triangular-section telson.
One cheliceral pair plus six similarly constructed walking-leg pairs. No Offacolus/Dibasterium branched brush exopods. Walking feet end in pointed claw/spurs, not six large pincer pairs.

Ventral transverse blade-feet with short marginal teeth/lamellar suggestion; use conservative six-group published restoration, mark number inference. At least3confirmed in2005 specimen;1981 could identify4inone specimen, neither proves complete6.

diagnostic_targets: High rounded laterally compressed helmet crest above skull; smooth arched outline with broad base on skull, no long backward tube and no separate posterior hatchet spike.
Broad duckbill, long neck, deep torso, powerful hindlimbs, shorter forelimbs and long tapering stiff balancing tail.
Entire animal in low balanced bipedal pose, tail raised clear of ground and forearms below shoulders, not an upright tail-dragging kangaroo.

frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Whole-organism reconstruction of Neusticosaurus edwardsii, historically called Pachypleurosaurus; not a specimen scan or isolated skull.

scientific_limits.en: Body proportions are interpreted from compressed museum skeleton photographs. The 1.25m total is a published estimate for IPZ3935, not a measurement of either photographed specimen. Flesh depth, webbing and coloration are inferred; no skin outline is asserted. Historical Pachypleurosaurus is retained as the inventory identity, not a separate valid genus or additional animal.
scientific_limits.zh: 依据压扁的博物馆骨架照片复原完整动物。1.25米是IPZ3935的文献估计，并非两张照片所示标本的实测长度。肉体厚度、蹼和颜色属推定，不声称保存了皮肤轮廓。保留历史清单名Pachypleurosaurus，但不将其视为另一有效属或另一动物。

taxonomy_and_scope_correction.revised_scale: 1.25m representative adult estimate from Paul IPZ3935, not forced into a hand-sized toy. Original inventory genus-specific size unverified. Small head is relative to elongated body; do not artificially miniaturize skull beyond actual bones.

evidence_anchors.size: Paul Princeton public table: Neusticosaurus edwardse IPZ3935 1.25m/5.4kg. Typographic species spelling in table preserved in source; accepted edwardsii in brief.
evidence_anchors.uncertainty: Do not identify either museum specimen as IPZ3935. No total-caliper metric on photo; scale is material-level author estimate. Opposite limbs partly occluded/disarticulated; use bilateral symmetry not missing limbs.

scale.basis: Paul size table IPZ3935, author estimate. Photographs supply same-species proportions, not specimen-calibrated total.
scale.interpretation: Partitions are approximate normalized photographic silhouette estimates, not independent caliper measurements. Photographed body straightened conservatively; do not retain postmortem neck U bend.

morphology: Whole slender lizardlike aquatic reptile, very small low narrow head relative to body, gently pointed rounded snout and recognizable eyes. Skull anterior region longer than posterior orbital region per2022 comparison; not broad Simosaurus crushing head, not needlelike ichthyosaur rostrum.
Long fine neck narrower than torso but not swan-necked plesiosaur. Neck about0.23m versus0.40m trunk; smoothly join the compact narrow ribcage. No inflated whale torso.

Exactly four short sprawling limbs with readable upper/lower joints and five short digit tips per hand/foot. Conservative partial webbing is inferred, not direct tissue evidence. No smooth boneless paddles, no exaggerated hyperphalangy or oversized claws.
Forelimbs slightly more robust than hindlimbs as museum skeletons suggest, not four enormous wings. Bilaterally paired, keep negative spaces at axilla and groin.
Long continuously tapering muscular tail around40%total, no flukes, dorsal fin or ornamental crest. Keep thin terminaltail visible without reproducing breaks in slab.
Near-horizontal gentle swimming posture; neutral closed or almost-closed jaws, no need to invent giant teeth. Cover bone gaps and eye sockets with living tissues.
Muted grey-brown with lighter belly, inferred coloration. No slab, fossil cracks, mount, labels, habitat or props.
must_not: Do not copy Prosantosaurus, Serpianosaurus, Keichousaurus or Lariosaurus soft anatomy.
Do not claim direct webbing/skin evidence or a measured1.25m photo specimen.
Do not reproduce historical name as separate species or make a second Neusticosaurus asset.

anatomy: Smooth laterally compressed shrimp-like carapace with anterior eye notch, paired stalked eyes and narrow rostrum about0.59ofcarapace, not the carapace-length rostrum of Lobetelson.
Six distinct curved abdominal somites with deep ventrally pointed pleura and subtle anterior excavations. First five carry paired simplified swimming flaps, sixth carries tail fan.

Eight paired robust single-branched thoracic walking limbs. Relatively stout intermediate joints, long merus/propodus; no giant lobster chelae and no added maxilliped pair. Two paired anterior antennal systems, fine flagella simplified.

Tail has strongly sclerotized blade-like outer uropods and spined inner rami, not broad rounded paddles. Outer ramus about1.5timesinner. Central narrow triangular telson tapers abruptly near distalquarter, with paired rearward small furcal projections.
restoration_boundaries: Real MPM P25899.1/.2 counterpart photographs document body curvature, segment outline and visible appendages. They have unlabeled scale bars; filename5cm is not accepted as a calibrated measurement. Do not apply PRI76753 4.5cm to this specimen.
2025 Figure5 ONLY panels1and6 are target species restoration. Panel2 BearGulch quoted magister is probably different species, panels3and7 B.traquairi, panels4/5/8 Lobetelson; never mix these.

2006 Figure1 ONLY panelC is target tail; large whole-body panelA and broadtailB are Lobetelson and must not be copied. The published reconstruction supplies missing anatomy, not a claim all features survive in MPM P25899.

Original generic broad tail fan is superseded by revised blade/spike fan diagnosis while retaining complete original organism and period. Muted color and standing/swimming pose are artistic, not pigment evidence.

scientific_limits.en: Living reconstruction, not a fossil scan. Nine metres is an NHM taxon estimate, not measured length of the illustrated individuals. scale.basis: NHM Dino Directory estimate; no scale transfer between museum mounts and ROM cranium.

diagnostic_targets: Low wide transverse solid crest over the eyes, slightly forward-facing concave dish, not a narrow sagittal blade or two separate horns.
Broad blunt spoon-like bill and deep jaw; head retains long face and distinct orbit region.
Deep robust trunk, neck, four limbs and long tapering tail retained; quadrupedal neutral stance with smaller forelimbs and elevated balancing tail.
Mature crest chosen from ROM66180 reference; do not substitute crestless juvenile or tall Corythosaurus helmet.
No sail, nose balloon, armour or exaggerated head spike; uncertain skin represented simply.
frozen_scientific_scope.specimen_basis: ROM66180 anterior/anterodorsal cranium Fig4 McFeeters etal2021 supports adult crest; MOR adult skull photograph supports bill. Wyoming Dinosaur Center mounted whole skeleton supports body anatomy; no unverified accession identity asserted.

diagnostic_targets: Long narrow pointed toothless bill, no broad spatulate duck bill and no teeth.
Distinct small rounded braincase and slender slightly curved neck connecting to streamlined oval trunk.
Complete paired feathered wings folded along body, not penguin flippers or flightless stubs.
Strong rear-positioned hindlimbs with readable bent joints and long swimming toes; feet drive diving, not wings.
Short feathered tail, body and hindleg proportions follow author silhouette, not a generic mallard or giant penguin.

frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Whole-organism adult Stenopterygius quadriscissus reconstruction, principally anchored to SMF R457; not a specimen scan.

scientific_limits.en: SMF R457 preserves a body and fin outline, but compression, preparation and missing tissues limit its fidelity. Published approximate total lengths differ: about2.3m in the2007 figure caption versus2.1m in Paul supplementary estimates. Use2.3m nominal, not exact caliper truth. Body width and external eye size are inferred. Countershading and scaleless integument are supported at genus level by partial MH432; exact hue is unknown. Purported microscopic collagen fibres in SMF R457 were questioned in2017 and are not reconstructed.
scientific_limits.zh: SMF R457保存体形和鳍轮廓，但压扁、修理和缺损限制其精确性。2007图注约2.3米与Paul估值2.1米不同，采用2.3米名义尺度而非精密实测。体宽和外眼大小推定；部分标本MH432支持属级无鳞皮肤及反荫蔽，确切色调未知。2017对SMF R457所谓胶原纤维提出质疑，不据此复原微观纹理。

evidence_anchors.primary_whole: Lingham-Soliar & Plodowski2007 Fig1: actual SMF457 whole fossil photo, publisher public image610x214. Entire snout, body, dorsal/caudal silhouette and near-side fore/hindlimb visible. No figure lineart substituted for original photograph.
evidence_anchors.soft_tissue: Lindgren et al2018 Nature public abstract/fig1: MH432 partialbody with scaleless integument and blubber; distribution ofmelanophores suggests countershading. Not wholebody/fin proportion source and not confidently assigned same species.
evidence_anchors.dentition: Dick & Maxwell2015 actualpaper: S.quadriscissus adult dental reduction. Fig1B SMNS53001 mandible523.2mm differentindividual. Closed mouth appropriate, not large protruding fang rows.
evidence_anchors.secondary_display: Haplochromis2009 Aquazoo adult/juvenile display: may incorporate cast/restored silhouette; never treat its smooth outline as originalskin or accessionSMF457. Supplementary comparison only, do not copy inflated displayed body.
evidence_anchors.preservation_limits: Flattenedfossil lacks living transversewidth. Dorsal/uppercaudal membranes shown, vertebralaxis enters lowerlobe. Four pairedflippers inwholeanimal even if far-side ones hidden. No supporting rods or matrix.

scale.basis: 2007 Fig1 public indexedcaption says approximately2.3m SMF457; Paul tableSMF4572.1m. Do not average or claim measured accuracy.
scale.interpretation: All subordinate dimensions are approximate visual ratios from SMF457 photo normalized to2.3m; not separately measured fossil values. Preorbital/jaw ratioaround0.65 must remain less elongated than Leptonectes comparator, while still an ichthyosaur beak, not a blunt dolphin face.

morphology: Whole compact fusiform streamlined body with narrow pointed matching upper/lowerjaws and large but not protruding eye. Snout relatively shorter than long-rostrum ichthyosaur examples, not truncated into genericdolphin.

Relatively narrow elongated foreflippers: span/chord about2.3–3.0, smoothly tapered roundpoint. Fourflippers exactly: forepairlarger, hindpairsmaller. No visibledigits, fingerwebs or fish finrays. Avoid broad ovals or oversizedflippers.
Full shortneck integrated into thickfront torso, tapering posteriorbody and narrowtailpeduncle. Lowpolyfacets are stylization not scales.
Single distinct triangular swept dorsalfin near midtrunk. Tall vertical lunate tail: uppermembranous lobe and downturned vertebral-supported lowerlobe. No horizontal cetacean fluke, no shark gills.
Closed fine jaw seam, adult teeth not protruding as hugefangs. Smooth skin with darkslate dorsal and palebelly countershading; exactshade/boundarypartlyinferred.
Neutral gently swimming pose. No wound, embryo, juvenilecompanion, fossilslab, exposedbones, labelorprops.
must_not: Do not claim MH432 is complete or its skin directly proves every finoutline.
Do not sculpt controversial collagen fibres or copy preparationmarks.
Do not use mature toothreduction as soleidentity distinction or changejawlengthjustforgate.
Do not copy museum reconstructeddisplaycontour as direct fossilskin.

distinctness_gate.required_combination: Relatively shorter rostrum + narrow elongated foreflippers + stronglyfusiformbody with substantialdorsalfin and lunatetail. Name,size,pose alone insufficient.

comparators.contrast: Its OUMJ10305 snout ratio0.72, elongatedneedlejaws and weaklyflexedtail; candidate inferredpreorbital/jaw~0.65 with morecompacthead/trunk and stronglylunatefin. Do not widenforeflippers to compensate.
Verylongupperjaw and lowerjawaroundhalf skull length. Candidate upper/lowernearlyequal; compactrostrum and smallerrelativeforeflippers.
Slender earlybody withlowdorsalfin andsmalluppercaudallobe. Candidatefullyfusiform withhighdorsal/lunatetail, not merely rescaleMixosaurus.

acceptance_focus: Lateralhead/torso ratio andforeflipper taper match SMF457withinvisible uncertainty.
Full originalcombination distinct from three comparators; not solecolour/size/pose.

scientific_limits.en: Canadian P.cooperi identification follows Laville et al2026; later2026 reassessment revises historical shield interpretations, so species-level ornamentation remains uncertain. GSC12858 measurements are real published data; abdomen, living depth and pose are approximate. Main paper locality age wording and Figure2 caption conflict; only Carboniferous is asserted.
scientific_limits.zh: 加拿大材料按Laville等2026鉴定为P.cooperi；后续2026修订指出历史背甲解释问题，因此种级饰纹仍存疑。GSC12858尺度来自真实公开数据，腹部比例、活体厚度及姿势为估计。论文产地年代正文与图2题注不一致，仅主张石炭纪。

frozen_scientific_scope.taxon: Pygocephalus; Canadian material identified as P. cooperi by Laville et al.2026

scale.uncertainty: First five values bound to GSC12858 data, rounded precision is not added accuracy. Wholebody excludes antennae and limbs, estimated about44mm; missing body depth and appendage posture inferred.

anatomy: Broad nearly circular shield, wider than long, short straight rostrum about0.26shieldlength, smaller paired anterolateral spines, curved lateral outline and concave posterior margin. Canadian reference lacks obvious lateral spine row; do not add unrelated species ornament.

Eight thoracic appendage pairs: first two compact feeding-associated pairs with enlarged bases; pairs3-8 longer walking limbs, increasing posteriorly. Do not model eight equal longlegs or modern five-pair decapod.

Six broad abdominal tergites with compact ringed profile, followed by distinct hexagonal telson. Uropods paired oval blades; telson bears two pairs of small ellipsoidal lobes plus central terminalspine, not onepair as Anthracaris.

Two paired anterior antennal systems, long fine flagella and flattened scaphocerites; small eyes conservatively reconstructed from2022species diagram, not declared preserved inGSC12858. Ventral firsttwo sternites obscured by feeding bases, later sternites broaden posteriorly.
restoration_boundaries: GSC12858 Figure2 is actual anchor, published numerical table linked directly by Zenodo GSC12858.csv. Figure2A bar5mm; detailbars3mm. Do not turn displaced broken fragment gaps into living anatomy.
GSC12810 and12811 Figure3 are same-paper appendage comparators, not the sameindividual;5mm bars separate. Preserve this composite boundary.

2022 Figure10 onlyD/F target dorsal and putative male ventral interpretation;A-C are Anthracaris. E is female with broodplates, not our default. Old dotted dorsal ornament is not copied over the smoother Canadian anchor.
Later Astrop2026 taxonomy article indexed text obtained but fullpage403; no bypass or claim fullrevision checked. Keep genus-level product name and explicit species determination uncertainty.
Paper Figure2 caption says lateVisean-Serpukhovian/Mabou, studiedmaterial text saysBashkirian/Parrsboro. Do not invent reconciliation or exactage. Carboniferous satisfies original scope.
Living depth, regularized symmetry, softparts and muted color are interpretive. No borrowed texture or copied scientific mesh.

frozen_scientific_scope.taxon: Plateosaurus trossingensis (older anatomical source uses P. engelhardti)

scale.basis: NHM taxon estimate; adult range independently described as 5-10 m by University of Bonn.

diagnostic_targets: Pear-shaped trunk with deeper broad pelvis/abdomen and narrowing chest, not uniform sauropod barrel.
Long gently curved neck with small elongate head, long tapering counterbalance tail.
Two robust weight-bearing hindlimbs; shorter arms held free with inward-facing palms, never flat weight-bearing pronated hands.
Five manual digits with clearly enlarged curved digit-I thumb claw; reduced outer digits, not five identical spikes.
Complete animal with readable negative spaces around elbows, neck and tail; original shape combination must survive comparison with Massospondylus and Mussaurus.
frozen_scientific_scope.specimen_basis: Adult mounted GPIT/RE/7288 on right in Mallison2014 photo; published digital study supplements skull and hand with other named specimens, not claimed single untouched skeleton. Fabian juvenile auxiliary photo is visibly separate.

scale.status: Skull approximate image-ruler estimate: about6.4 times labeled5mm. Head-body110mm and tail60mm artistic proportions using museum reconstruction, not complete fossil measurements.

diagnostic_targets: Slender elongated low snout, visible transition to somewhat wider posterior skull, not globular short mouse face.
Low elongated furry torso with four short limbs and readable elbow/knee bends; not specialized digging forearms or hopping hindlimbs.
Slender tapering moderately long balancing tail, not a paddle, squirrel plume or prehensile curl.
Small rounded external ears and modest eyes; soft anatomy inferred, not cartoon rodent ears.
Five small clawed digits per foot as conservative reconstruction; not primate grasping hands or cloven hooves.
Closed or almost closed mouth; if teeth shown, small differentiated insectivore teeth with canines, not enlarged paired rodent incisors.

description.en: {"representation":"living-reconstruction","scope":"Whole adult Ophthalmosaurus icenicus living reconstruction using documented British Oxford Clay skeletal material and explicitly inferred soft tissues; not a scan or single complete individual.","scientific_limits":{"en":"NHM display is a composite of R3702, R3893 and R4124, with historically reversed forelimbs: do not copy their orientation. frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Whole adult Ophthalmosaurus icenicus living reconstruction using documented British Oxford Clay skeletal material and explicitly inferred soft tissues; not a scan or single complete individual.

scientific_limits.en: NHM display is a composite of R3702, R3893 and R4124, with historically reversed forelimbs: do not copy their orientation. Senckenberg display has unquantified restoration and artificial fin silhouettes. Moon and Kirton measurements and Buchholtz axial data control anatomy; the4.5m scale is a published estimate for the NHM composite, not a measured complete individual. External eye aperture is smaller than the bony orbit. Dorsal fin, upper caudal lobe, transverse width and colors are inferred, not preserved skin of these specimens. Small teeth are not few teeth: roughly50 per jaw ramus, not edentulous.
scientific_limits.zh: NHM展架由R3702、R3893、R4124组成且前肢历史装反，不照抄朝向。森肯贝格展架修复比例不明，黑色鳍轮廓为人工展示。解剖以Moon与Kirton测量及Buchholtz轴骨资料控制；4.5米是NHM组合架公开估值，非完整个体实测。外眼开口小于骨眼眶。背鳍、尾上叶、体宽和颜色推定，非这些标本直接皮肤证据。小齿不等于少颗齿，每颌支约50颗而非无齿。

original_scope.en: Planned animal asset: very large eye region and a compact tooth-reduced snout.
original_scope.zh: 规划中的动物资产：极大眼区与紧凑少齿吻部。

original_description_correction.en: Interpret the inventory tooth-reduced phrase as reduced tooth size/visual prominence, not low tooth count. The snout remains slender and long, with a compact deep orbital region; do not truncate the beak to force the planning adjective compact. Whole-animal scope retained.
original_description_correction.zh: 将清单少齿理解为牙尺寸和外显程度减小，不是牙数量稀少。吻仍细长，眼区紧凑深大；不为清单紧凑形容词截短尖吻，保持全体范围。

evidence_anchors.cranial: Moon & Kirton2016 author accepted manuscript: R3013 orbit280mm / jaw1000mm=0.28; orbit faces slightly anteriorly. R3893 and GLAHM V1921 show approximately50 small teeth per ramus, not merely a few or no teeth.
evidence_anchors.whole_body: Captmondo2008 real NHM composite photograph shows deep ribcage, enormous orbit, four-limb layout but tail cropped. Ghedoghedo2011 Senckenberg entire mounted skeleton photograph provides complementary full axial/tail/limb layout. Neither is pristine single individual or original skin.
evidence_anchors.axial: Buchholtz2001 p65/Table1: PMAG R340 has101 vertebrae atlas to mid-fluke; precaudal estimate1040mm, longest rib0.79 precaudal, forelimb0.41 and hindlimb0.20 precaudal (partly reconstructed), tailstock0.65. Supports deep thunniform torso and strongly reduced hindfins. Neural spines usually restored; do not use mount heights as precise truth.
evidence_anchors.limb: Araujo et al2008 NMING F21787: actual fossil pectoral girdle and paddle material; Fig8A reconstruction, Fig8B original in situ Leeds drawing, both20cm scale. Humerus155mm, distalwidth140mm. This is an independent individual and scale cannot be silently combined into one measured specimen.
evidence_anchors.scale: Paul published table: NHMUK composite estimated total4.5m. Use nominal4.5m only; 6m general entry not this chosen target. No claim that R3013 and PMAG R340 are the4.5m composite.

scale.basis: Paul NHM composite estimate, not scan measurement
scale.interpretation: Subordinate model targets are artistic bounded estimates, not measured dimensions of the composite. Keep cranial orbit/jaw near0.28, external eye materially smaller; never expose a naked bone ring on a living model.

morphology: Deep compact fusiform torso and very large orbital region; pointed matching upper/lower narrow jaws. Short neck concealed within streamlined head-trunk transition. No dolphin bulbous forehead.

Two foreflippers plus two substantially smaller hindflippers, no visible free fingers. Foreflippers broader relative to their length than Stenopterygius narrow paddles; use documented skeletal layout, not historically reversed NHM mounting.
Eyes large but seated in flesh, slightly anterior-facing. External visible aperture smaller than0.28 jaw-length bony orbit; no cartoon protruding globe and no exposed sclerotic ring.
Closed thin jaw seam with teeth visually inconspicuous; retain actual tiny-toothed interpretation, no giantfangs, no fictional near-toothlessness.

Single inferred swept triangular dorsal fin and vertical heterocercal crescent tail with vertebral axis downturned into lowerlobe. Upper membrane inferred, not original fossil silhouette. No horizontal whale fluke.
Restrained dark-gray dorsum and lighter underside are plausible artistic countershading, not taxon-specific known color. Smooth skin approximation, no scale armor, gills, stands or exposedbones.

shape_gate.required_combination: Large orbital region + unobtrusive small-toothed narrow beak + deep compact torso, preserving wholeanimal. Must distinguish from Stenopterygius by geometry, not size/color/pose.
shape_gate.comparison: Private frozen Stenopterygius descriptor and actual SMF457 photo are self-contained. Stenopterygius target bonyorbit/jaw0.095/0.49≈0.194 and narrow forefin span/chord2.3–3.0; Ophthalmosaurus supported bonyorbit/jaw0.28 plus deeper body and broader forefins. External eye cannot equal full orbit in either animal.
acceptance: Lateral shows relatively much larger orbital region without shortening the real pointedbeak.
Deep broad torso, robust head-eye transition and broad forepaddles distinguish the compact combination from slender Stenopterygius.
Four paired fins, much smaller hindpair, verticaltail/dorsalfin visible; no reversed mount artifact.
No invented tooth loss or massivefangs. Externaleyes fleshed-over and smaller than orbitalregion.

frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Complete Carboniferous living scorpion, anchored to NMS G.1987.7.136 with missing appendages interpreted using Dunlop and Garwood 2024 Figure 9, third animal. Not a fossil slab or a modern scorpion substitute.

scientific_limits.en: Approximate dimensions estimated from the 10 cm bar of specimen NMS G.1987.7.136, not direct measurements or the popular giant maximum. The specimen is fragmented; symmetry, missing limbs, living depth, upward tail pose and color are inferred. Published genus reconstruction guides absent appendages.
scientific_limits.zh: 尺度由 NMS G.1987.7.136 标本照片的 10 厘米图尺估算，不是实测，也不采用网络巨型上限。标本有碎裂，左右对称、缺失附肢、活体厚度、上弯尾姿与颜色为推断；缺失部分参考公开同属复原。

scale.uncertainty: Approximate photo-bar estimates, about 15-20 percent; total excludes pedipalps and legs and measures tail centerline, not posed bounding box.

anatomy: Broad ribbed mesosoma with seven dorsal tergites; approximately rectangular carapace with anterior median eye prominence interpreted from target Figure 9. Do not copy lateral compound eyes of the second animal, Proscorpius.

A pair of small anterior chelicerae, one pair of long pedipalps ending in slender fingers and modest palms, and four pairs of walking legs. Walking legs progressively reach farther posteriorly; do not copy digitigrade tapering Palaeophonus legs.

Five distinct articulated metasomal segments followed by a separate bulbous telson with curved sting. Tail held gently upward in life interpretation, with rounded joints rather than fossil fragment gaps.
Pedipalp chela fingers long relative to small palm. Do not turn into short massive modern emperor scorpion pincers. Broad dorsum and long segmented tail preserve original visual gate.

Ventral coxae remain close to sternum as mesoscorpion group A described by Jeram; do not expose internal book lungs as external organs. Tiny uncertain ventral details simplified rather than fabricated.
restoration_boundaries: Actual NMS specimen is fragmented and appendages displaced. Fossil gaps and detached pincer are taphonomic, not live anatomical segmentation. No claim of complete single-specimen preservation.
NMS G.1987.7.136 is not asserted to be a holotype; official type-status field does not establish that. Visean, East Kirkton Quarry, Bed 47.
2024 Figure 9 third animal is a scholarly genus-level whole-animal interpretation, not the NMS specimen scan. Other three genera are excluded.
Original Jeram abstract accessed; full paywalled text not claimed read. PeerJ and PMC access blocked, no bypass; independently accessible attributed CC-BY Figure 9 was inspected.
Depth, leg joint pose, tail upcurve and muted brown coloration are interpretation. Do not infer exact color or eye-lens count from black diagram.
BGS photographs and scientific diagrams remain private research; no borrowed mesh or image texture in product.

frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Complete adult with large thumb spikes, deep body and broad weight-bearing hands. No juvenile, isolated hand or skeletal-display substitution.

scientific_limits.en: Living reconstruction, not fossil scan. Ten metres is an NHM taxon estimate within the Belgian institute adult range, not measured length of photographed R51. Original upright mounts and burial drawings do not prescribe living posture. Soft tissues and colours are interpretative; exact gait remains debated.
scientific_limits.zh: 完整成体活体复原，非扫描化石。10米为博物馆物种估值，非照片R51实测全长。旧直立装架和埋藏线描不规定活体姿态；软组织颜色为推断，精确步态仍有争论。

scale.basis: NHM10m estimate; Belgian institute adult range9-11m. Not museum mount bounding length.

frozen_scientific_scope.specimen_basis: IRSNB R51 holotype described on Belgian institute collection page; associated museum gallery photo and original Lavalette lettre A fossil drawing. Separate museum-published hand photo has no accession asserted.
diagnostic_targets: Deep heavy trunk with strong hindquarters, long stiff tapering tail and elongated low beaked head.
Robust shorter forelimbs support a neutral quadrupedal stance with subhorizontal back; no kangaroo tripod or tail dragging.
Each hand has a conspicuous conical digit-I spike distinct from load-bearing digits II-IV and a separate flexible digit V.
Three central fingers form broad compact hoof-like load-bearing unit; not human palm splay, not five identical clawed toes.
No nasal horn or cranial crest. Maintain complete torso, neck, tail and four limbs; not gracile Mantellisaurus.

scientific_limits.en: Whole living reconstruction, not an articulated single specimen or scan. AMNH1480 skull and LACM3342/42889 skeletal mount are separate references. scale.status: Skull approximate image-ruler projection from AMNH1480 (10cm bar), not caliper measurement. Wholebody and tail estimates use AMNH pony-size description and skeletal proportions; perspective mount not used as exact ruler.

diagnostic_targets: Slender long limbs with substantial clearance below ribcage, unlike a barrel-bodied short-legged Teleoceras or hippo-like Metamynodon.
No nasal or frontal horn: smooth nasal silhouette.
Three distinct short hoofed toes on all FOUR feet, broad central toe and smaller flanking toes; not horse single hoof.
Moderately long neck and relatively large deep-cheeked head with constricted muzzle, not tiny deer head or giant Paraceratherium neck.
Compact non-barrel torso, visible shoulder/hip limb transitions, thin moderately long tail.
Conservative neutral coat, no exact copying of artist striping or unsupported horn/tusk ornament.

frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Whole adult Cyamodus hildegardis reconstruction, combining explicitly identified specimens T4763 and T58 from the same species; skeletal evidence plus bounded soft-tissue inference, not a fossil scan or skull-only substitute.

scientific_limits.en: The adult fossils are incomplete and disturbed. Two shields and four-row tail armour have direct fossil support, but shield interiors and original separation are uncertain. Carapace size is directly grounded in T58; total length and head/tail proportions are inferred from Scheyer2010 reconstruction, not an intact measured individual. Feet are unknown in this species; five short minimally webbed tips are a conservative tetrapod inference, not preserved anatomy. Body depth, eye aperture, soft skin and colors are inferred. No ventral plastron is supported.
scientific_limits.zh: 成人标本不完整且有移位。双盾及四列尾甲有真化石依据，盾内甲片布置和原间距不确定。主甲尺度依据T58；总长及头尾比例据Scheyer2010复原推算，不称完整个体实测。本种足部未知，五短指与最低限度蹼缘仅四足类保守推定而非保存解剖。体高、外眼、皮肤和颜色推定，无腹甲证据。

original_scope.en: Planned animal asset: two-part armored shell and a compact broad head.
original_scope.zh: 规划中的动物资产：两部分组成的甲壳与紧凑宽头。

frozen_scientific_scope.taxonomic_note: Use C.hildegardis as Scheyer2010 and Gere et al2024. Earlier proposed synonymy with C.laticeps/C.muensteri is acknowledged, not used to import another species anatomy or create another asset. ID remains cyamodus.

evidence_anchors.whole: Scheyer2010 Fig2 actual photographs: PIMUZ T4763 holotype dorsal and PIMUZ T58 ventral,10cm bars. Fig3 juvenile MSNM V458 is a cast, not primary adult photo. These are articulated but incomplete/disturbed, not complete pristine bodies.
evidence_anchors.armour: Figs4–8 real photos plus separately labelled interpretative drawings establish large near-round maincarapace, separate smaller pelvicshield, decreasing tailplates. Fig9 is author LIFE RECONSTRUCTION, not fossil photograph; Fig10.1 is revised anatomical synthesis, Fig10.2 the old comparison to avoid copying.
evidence_anchors.skull: Neil Pezzoni2021 actual PIMUZ T4763 skull photograph, same holotype as Fig2.1; short broadly triangular posterior skull and compact rostrum. Fossil fractures/temporal openings are not skinholes.
evidence_anchors.scale: Table1 T58 specimen approx215mm long ×230mm wide; interpretative Fig10.1 approx205×215mm. Adopt205×215mm nominal living mainshield, with observed measurement uncertainty stated.
evidence_anchors.current_taxon: Gere et al2024 open article continues C.hildegardis and studies placodont crushing dentition. Do not adopt historical speculative herbivory or mix cranial anatomy from other listed genera.

scale.basis: Mainshield dimension measured/estimated in Scheyer2010 Table1. Other dimensions are approximate model targets from Fig9 interpreted shape normalized to205mm mainshield; not independent fossil measurements. Do not use Paul0.75m T58 entry labelled muensteri as taxonomic authority.

morphology: Whole compact low-bodied aquatic reptile, not a turtle or broad ray: main near-circular shallowly domed oval shield about0.95 length/width; separate smaller pelvic shield behind it.

Maintain a narrow flexible skin band between shields, visible especially fromtop/oblique. No detached floating shell and no through-body hole; fossil postmortem separation must not become exaggerated live gap.

Mainshield has small enlarged triangular/scalloped lateral plates of broadly similar size; pelvicshield sideplates taper posteriorly. Avoid enormous sawblade spikes or front carapace horns. Interior tile layout is simplified uncertain armour, not a claimed turtle scute formula.

Short broad triangular head with compact snout and fleshed-over temporal region; no Placochelys needle-like beak and no Henodus transverse square shovel muzzle. Closed mouth with no protrudingfangs; crushing teeth internal.

Short exposed neck, four short splayed limbs under lateral shell margins. Feet unknown: five short rounded minimally webbed tips each are explicitly inferred; do not create sea-turtle flippers or assert fossil phalangealformula.
Tapering short tail relative to long-tailed placodonts, with four diminishing armour rows: one dorsal, one ventral and two lateral. No tailclub, dorsalfin or fishfluke.

No belly plastron: soft ventral surface with gastral support not externally exposed bones. No specimen slab, labels or skeleton openings. Muted brown-gray keratinous armour and subdued lighter skin are artistic inferred colors.

shape_gate.required_combination: Two distinct dorsal armour units plus compact broad head, whole organism retained.
shape_gate.comparisons: Henodus: single very broad rectangular carapace and square transverse head versus Cyamodus near-round mainshield plus pelvicshield and triangular compact head. Placochelys: elongated single carapace interpretation and long toothless rostrum versus shorter broad head and splitshield. ScheyerTable1 directly contrasts ratios0.95 Cyamodus,0.77 Henodus,1.4 Placochelys (last is interpretation only).
acceptance: Top and perspective must plainly show large mainshield and separate smaller pelvicshield with narrow skin joint, not a colored seam on a single turtle shell.
Head broad posteriorly and compact triangular, not the Henodus square snout or Placochelys elongatedrostrum.
Tail has decreasing armour rows, four complete limbs, no plastron or flipper substitution.
Do not mistake Fig1 oldsinglearmor or Fig10.2 oldoverbroad reconstruction for the selected evidence.

scientific_limits.en: The brownii anchor preserves spine bases, not complete long branches. Branching spines are a same-genus interpretation using armigera descriptions and family topology, not a claim that brownii preserved them. Antennae, minute head details, pose and color are inferred. Body length and width follow historical measurements of the real specimen.

frozen_scientific_scope.taxon: Euphoberia, genus-level interpretation anchored to E. brownii holotype

scale.uncertainty: Four inches long, nearly quarter-inch wide, 36 rings in Woodward brownii account. Width rounded; spine lengths/depth are conservative genus-level proportions, not brownii measurements. Do not use family maximum30cm.

anatomy: Long cylindrical articulated body, 36 raised rings used as historical trunk-ring guide, small rounded head and modest terminal region. Gently curved pose keeps all rings readable; not flattened Arthropleura armor.

Two paired sets of metazonal spines: lateral pair plus subdorsal pair on regular trunk rings, making four longitudinal rows. Lateral spines visibly fork with a small secondary branch; not rows of unbranched needles only.

Paired walking legs under diplosegments, two pairs per ordinary trunk diplosegment. Apodous collum and anterior single-pair transition follow diplopod anatomy; do not put two pairs on the head/collum or turn into centipede single-pair trunk.
Small anterior antenna pair and simplified rounded head are reconstructed, not directly established by the fragmentary brownii head. No Arthropleura-shaped head, predatory jaws or scorpion pincers.
Subtle corrugation of rings; no massive flat lateral plates. Small eyes optional simplified dark points, not claimed lens arrangement.
restoration_boundaries: NMS G.1884.46.180, BGS-listed E. brownii holotype, Kilmaurs coal measures. Actual photo P889185 has 5cm bar and was inspected; not a 3D mesh source.

Woodward original account reports36 rings, four-inch length and nearlyquarter-inch breadth; modern paired-leg organization overrides obsolete literal two ventral segments terminology. Ring count is historical and may omit small terminal/anterior elements, not a newly measured count.
Woodward compares E. armigera and describes branched spines; this comparison supplies same-genus missing anatomy only. No claim all armigera anatomy belongs to brownii.
Wilson and Anderson2004 family diagnosis supplies lateral/subdorsal paired spine positions and head/coxal guidance. Do not copy unrelated Archidesmus or Pneumodesmus figures from that paper.

Carnegie museum diorama photo is a secondary interpretive silhouette comparator, not specimen measurement or direct fossil evidence. Its color is not fossil truth and its poorly resolved spine branches must not replace primary text.
Long spines, exact branch angles, living thickness, missing extremities and color remain explicitly interpretive; no new precise species diagnosis or generic maximum size.

scale.status: 555mm premaxilla-occipital measured in 2023 Table3 UNISTRA.2015.0.1106. Fullbody artist estimate from skeletal outline, not same-specimen measurement; avoid presenting 3m as measured.

diagnostic_targets: Heavy elongate broad torso with deep ribs and short stout limbs; not slender Hyracodon or high-legged running rhino.
Broad cheek and short facial region with eyes high on the skull; restrained rounded ears and thickened upper lip inferred, no long tapir trunk.
Clearly visible paired enlarged canine tips near mouth front, upper canines downwards, restrained lower canines upwards; no saber-cat fangs or elephant tusks.
Absolutely no nasal/frontal horn. Low smooth head profile with a modest fleshed posterior crest, not a tall horn.
Four functional hoofed toes on EACH forefoot, three on EACH hindfoot; do not inherit Hyracodon three-front-toe count.
Substantial neck, broad rump, tapering tail, restrained gray-brown skin with no armor plating.

scale.basis: Historical holotype estimate cited in2017redescription; complete adult length unknown. Tail tip extrapolated, not measured.

diagnostic_targets: Long tall continuous dorsal profile extends from back across sacrum onto proximal tail, with higher dorsal and lower sacral rise rather than a single triangular fin.
Elongated low broad-ended beaked head, modest paired nasal bulges; no theropod jaws or cranial horn.
Deep herbivorous trunk, shorter forelimbs and strong hindlimbs, long tapering tail retained.
Sail is covered soft tissue around neural spines, not exposed bone bars, separate plates, or an invented camel hump.
Small hands remain conservative because complete manus is not preserved; no exaggerated Iguanodon thumb weapons.

frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Complete Carboniferous trigonotarbid: compact pear-shaped outline, triangular carapace, broad divided dorsal abdominal plates and no tail. Based on actual NHMUK I.15860 fossil/CT and same-species idealized reconstruction.

scientific_limits.en: Published dimensions belong to scanned NHMUK I.15860, not the smaller holotype. Symmetry, absent distal limb portions, living posture and color are interpretations guided by the same-species reconstruction. No venom, silk structures or long tail inferred.
scientific_limits.zh: 公开尺度属于扫描标本 NHMUK I.15860，不是较小的正模。左右对称、缺失肢端、活体姿态和颜色为参考同种复原的解释；不臆造毒腺、吐丝结构或长尾。

scale.uncertainty: Body and leg4 values published for NHMUK I.15860. Depth and regularized pose inferred; do not use holotype4.8mm body or2.5mm abdomen width.

anatomy: Triangular carapace widens posteriorly with smooth unlobed sides, raised median ridge, small anterior rounded clypeus and close median eyes. Shallow inverted-T depression behind eyes joins rear transverse groove.

Broad rounded opisthosoma with central and lateral dorsal plates. Tergite1 is a ridge partly tucked beneath carapace; tergites2 and3 remain separate, not fused diplotergite; narrow tergite9 not laterally divided.
Four pairs of short robust jointed walking legs plus separate slender pedipalps and small downward-hanging chelicerae under clypeus. Pedipalps are not a fifth walking pair and not long antennae.
Leg4 proportions follow measured six distal podomeres; short metatarsus and longer tarsus. Coxae meet small diamond-shaped sternum; no large pedipalp pincers.
Ventral sternites curve backwards, especially posteriorly; sternites9+10 apparently fused with small ventral pygidium near their anterior edge. Pygidium is not a projecting external tail.
Generally smooth surface without major spines or pustules. No spider spinnerets, narrow spider waist, scorpion sting, Eophrynus spines or fused shield over all abdomen.
restoration_boundaries: Actual hand fossil panels in Figure2 and CT Figure3 specifically identify NHMUK I.15860; Figure4 is an idealized same-species synthesis using that scan and additional hand specimens. Do not call Figure4 photograph or complete preservation.
Holotype NHMUK In31239 is distinct and4.8mm long. Model anchors scanned6.3mm specimen; keep their measurements separate.
Late Carboniferous Coseley near Dudley, UK. Figure3 missing/irregular parts are taphonomic or segmentation artifacts, not living gaps.
Reconstructed symmetry and limb posture follow Figure4, not copied CT mesh. Living thickness estimated; muted color artistic.
Tergite1 ridge and narrow undivided9 prevent blindly making nine identical tripartite rows. Keep exact declared segment topology inspectable.

frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Whole Placodus gigas living reconstruction using Senckenberg original skeletal remains, supplementary reconstructed mount and species-specific tooth evidence. Not a single pristine complete skeleton or a specimen scan.

scientific_limits.en: The Senckenberg mount contains large missing intervals, especially the tail; Zurich is explicitly a reconstructed mount. Museum size1.5m and Paul estimated total3.2m differ and cannot be asserted as matching measurements: use3.2m nominal restored total, not precise measured length. Soft tissues, webbing, color and distal tail shape are inferred. A humerus historically included by Drevermann was reassigned to Nothosaurus by Rieppel1994 and must not be copied. Palatal specimen BSP1968I75 is a different individual, not the skeleton skull.
scientific_limits.zh: 森肯贝格架有大量缺段，尤其尾部，苏黎世明确是重建架。博物馆尺寸1.5米与Paul估计总长3.2米不同，不得宣称一致实测；采用3.2米名义补全总长而非精密长度。软组织、蹼、颜色及末尾形状推定。Drevermann纳入的一枚肱骨被Rieppel1994改归Nothosaurus，不照抄。BSP1968I75齿板为另一个体，不冒骨架同一头骨。

original_scope.en: Planned animal asset: deep barrel torso and projecting front teeth ahead of crushing plates.
original_scope.zh: 规划中的动物资产：深桶躯干与压碎齿板前方突出的前齿。

evidence_anchors.body: Daderot2012 photograph of original Senckenberg mounted bones: deep curved ribs/gastralia forming barrel trunk, short neck, four limb positions and single midline row of low round osteoderms. Missing bones/support rods are not anatomy.
evidence_anchors.complete_layout: NGPezz2021 Zurich reconstructed mount: supplementary full outline/limb layout only, not original complete fossil or independent measured scale. Retain uncertainty of reconstructed tail.
evidence_anchors.dentition: Gere et al2024 Fig1 actual BSP1968I75 palatal cranium,2cm bars: large flattened palatine and smaller marginal maxillary teeth. Text explicitly three premaxillary pairs, four maxillary pairs and three palatine pairs in P.gigas. Front teeth project forward, posterior crushing teeth not pointedfangs.
evidence_anchors.classification: Klein et al2022 supports P.gigas context but new isolated dentaries assigned only cf.gigas; do not adopt those as definitive same individual. Historical P.antiquior synonymy acknowledged.
evidence_anchors.limb_correction: Rieppel1994 Fig60A is Nothosaurus formerly attributed to Placodus; Fig60B SMNS59827 is P.gigas, C MHI776 Placodus. Neither rescales the whole model.
evidence_anchors.scale: Paul supplementary table SMF R1035 estimates3.2m; museum original exhibit lists1.5m without resolving full restored total vs preserved display extent. Record both, do not silently average or convert1.5 into an exact total.

scale.basis: Paul estimated complete length SMFR1035; museum size discrepancy retained and unresolved, not same measured quantity claimed.
scale.interpretation: Subordinate targets are conservative modeling ratios from original ribcage and reconstructed outline, not measurements of preserved individual. Tail uncertainty does not erase original deepbody/frontteethgate.

morphology: Deep rounded barrel torso with substantial ventral volume, short distinct neck and robust moderately elongated head. No flattening into a turtle shield or generic ichthyosaur fusiformbody.

Three pairs of short sturdy forward-projecting upper premaxillary teeth, chisel-like tips, not thin predatoryfangs or giantwalrustusks. Show them clearly in lateral and head-on views. Lower anterior dentition simplify conservatively as two pairs of short grasping teeth, a reconstructed working arrangement rather than a measured skeleton count.

Behind the anterior grasping teeth, four pairs of smaller flattened upper marginal teeth and three pairs of broad flat palatal crushing teeth. Do not turn the entire toothrow into pointedcrocodilefangs. Lower cheek dentition is rounded/flat crushing surfaces.
Modestly open jaws around20degrees to make frontteeth and posteriorflat crushing surfaces inspectable without grotesque gape; maintain thick lips/gums and fully fleshedhead, not bare skull.

Four stout splayed limbs ending in five short digits each, light partialwebbing inferred, no sea-turtle flippers. Keep elbows/knees and shortforearm transitions, do not recreate misassigned nothosaur bone.

Single row of low rounded dorsal osteoderms integrated along midline, not tallspines and not a broad shell. Long tapering muscular tail with no fishfluke/dorsalfin; restored length/terminalshape explicitly inferred.
Subdued gray-brown skin with slightly darker back and low osteoderms; exact color/scalation unknown. No specimen supports, exposedribs or extrahead.

shape_gate.required_combination: Deep barrel trunk plus conspicuous forward short anterior grasping teeth in front of broad posterior crushing surfaces, whole body retained.
shape_gate.comparisons: Cyamodus has two broad armour shields and compact broadhead; Placodus has no broadcarapace, a single low dorsalrow, deeper unshieldedbarrel and protrudingfrontteeth. Simosaurus has longerneck and different blunt-tooth arrangement, not the Placodus projectingchisel front plus palatal pavement.
acceptance: Lateral clearly deep barrel torso, shortneck and forward chisel-like frontteeth.
Head-on and perspective reveal anterior-to-posterior tooth differentiation without giantfangs.
Top shows no turtlecarapace/two-shield transplant; exactlyfour shortleggedlimbs and single low dorsalosteodermrow.
No Nothosaurus misassigned diagnostic limb copy, no precisionclaim on restoredtail or3.2m estimate.

frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Whole relatively gracile ground sloth with small elongated skull and long reaching forelimbs.

scientific_limits.en: Whole living reconstruction based on the partially mummified YPM13198 skeleton and published comparisons, not a scan. NPS approximate9ft total length is a species-level estimate, not a measured length of YPM13198. Preserved patches establish hair but complete coat pattern, ears, facial soft tissues and exterior digital padding are inferred. Historical specimen finger restoration is not unquestioned anatomical evidence; manual digitV lacks a claw according to2011 reassessment.

scale.status: Total rounded from NPS approximate9ft, not exact specimen measurement. Nose-rump/tail/skull are original proportional estimates from YPM13198 silhouette. Lull1929 p9 measured YPM maxilla-occipital287+mm,muzzle59.5mm; fleshed model head0.32m estimate.

diagnostic_targets: Small narrow elongated head and muzzle, not block-headed giant Megalonyx; closed mouth with no exposed incisors or caniniform tusks.
Relatively slender reaching forelimbs compared with stout bent hindlimbs; visible elbow and wrist transitions, not four massive elephant columns.
Arched back, deep but not giant spherical barrel, strong pelvis and long thick-based tapering tail.
Ground-walking low quadrupedal stance, hands curled inward and hindfeet supported laterally, not modern hanging tree-sloth limbs.
Three large manual claws II-IV, smaller medial digitI claw and reduced nonclawed digitV; do not copy historical incorrectly restored fifth claw.
Restrained short-to-moderate fur implied by facets; small ears and neutral sandy coat inferred, no invented sloth face mask.
Hindfeet II,III,IV each clawed: III largest, II intermediate, IV smaller curved inward; I externally absent and V reduced nonclawed. Lateral padded support, not five equal bear claws.

frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Whole living Nothosaurus mirabilis, proportions anchored to postcranial holotype UMO1000 with same-species skull comparisons. Reconstructed missing anatomy is explicit, not a single complete pristine skeleton or specimen scan.

scientific_limits.en: UMO1000 is a not fully grown incomplete skeleton: skull, shoulder girdle, posterior dorsals and distal tail are missing. Published restored total2.9–3.2m and inferred skull0.32m are estimates, not measurements of a complete animal. Skull photograph has no verified accession or restoration history; use it with actual SMNS59817 mandibular comparison, not as the holotype skull. Webbing, skin, color, complete feet, body thickness and missing tail tip are inferred. Do not copy N.giganteus, N.jagisteus, Simosaurus or modern sea-turtle fins.
scientific_limits.zh: UMO1000为未完全长成的不完整骨架，头骨、肩带、后躯干及末尾缺失。发表的补全总长2.9至3.2米及推测头长0.32米不是完整动物实测。头骨照片未核定编号与修复史，须结合SMNS59817真下颌比较，不冒充模式头骨。蹼、皮肤、颜色、完整脚形、软体厚度及尾尖推定；不得移植其他种属或海龟鳍。

original_scope.en: Planned animal asset: long fang-bearing head, sinuous neck and webbed limb plan.
original_scope.zh: 规划中的动物资产：长獠齿头、蜿蜒颈与蹼肢构型。

evidence_anchors.skeleton: Klein et al2022 actual Fig4 UMO1000 photographs20cm scale; Fig5 interpretative drawing. Fig3 historical cast is not original preserved full anatomy. Complete19-cervical neck,20 anterior dorsals, anterior caudal strings, humeri and right femur; posterior axial gaps explicit.
evidence_anchors.scale: 2022 body-size section: preserved axial strings212cm, inferred missing posterior dorsals23.5cm, estimated skull32cm and missing terminal tail20–50cm; authors estimate total290–320cm. Fig19 is a scaled RECONSTRUCTION, not photograph or independently measured whole specimen.
evidence_anchors.limbs: 2022 original humerus broad/wing-shaped and ulna flat; humerus-ulna ratio2.09. Femur comparatively slender with round-oval section. Digit/web envelope reconstruction conservative; no fossil skin claim.
evidence_anchors.head: Ghedoghedo2013 Tuebingen skull image attributed N.mirabilis shows long narrowed rostrum with anterior expansion and prominent pointed teeth. Rieppel1994 Fig3C actual N.mirabilis SMNS59817 symphysis20mm confirms elongate mandibular symphysis distinct from Fig3A Simosaurus. Neither is UMO1000 skull.
evidence_anchors.motion: 2022 large intercentral spaces and axial morphology support lateral undulation. Gentle lateral neck curve is plausible pose, not preserved fixed S-neck or demonstrated extreme flexibility.

scale.interpretation: Targets except explicitly preserved length are estimates chosen inside published restored range, not individual measurements. Curved pose reduces straight bounding-box length. Head and neck use published Fig19 estimates; remaining volumes/limbs simplified conservatively.

morphology: Elongate low head with narrow rostral waist and modest expanded terminal bulb, posterior head wider. Fleshed skull with paired eyes, not exposed temporal fenestrae. Do not substitute short broad unconstricted Simosaurus head.

Pointed slender grasping teeth, a few distinctly larger anterior/maxillary fangs among smaller marginal teeth; modestly open jaws12–18degrees keeps fang-bearing profile inspectable. Total count is simplified, not asserted as specimen dental formula; no saber tusks, no flat crushing plates.

Distinct neck approximately1.5times head centerline length, gradual muscular transition into long ribbed trunk. Gentle lateral bend about10–20degrees, no abrupt snake knot or plesiosaur-length neck. Shape not distinguishable by pose alone.

Four splayed jointed limbs, forelimbs broad proximally with visible elbow/short forearm transition and webbed distal feet; hindlimbs somewhat smaller/slenderer. Five conservative digit tips per foot with shallow intervening clefts and partial webbing inferred, not closed sea-turtle flippers.
Long tapering muscular tail continues axial line, no vertical fish fluke, no dorsal fin or armor shell. High neural spines buried in substantial dorsal soft tissue, not an invented exposed sail.
Restrained gray-brown coloration with lighter underside is artistic inference. Smooth low-poly flesh, no fossil slab/support rods or bare vertebrae.

shape_gate.required_combination: Long constricted fang-bearing head, distinct gently curving neck, jointed webbed four-limb plan and tapering tail, whole animal.
shape_gate.comparison: Simosaurus has broad short unconstricted head and blunt bulbous crowns. Nothosaurus must differ in rostral constriction/long symphysis and pointed prominent teeth, not just name, scale or neck pose. Lariosaurus has more compact short-necked proportions; do not reuse its body ratio.
acceptance: Lateral and perspective clearly show elongate head with obvious long pointed fangs, distinct neck and entire tail.
Top makes snout waist and anterior expansion readable versus broad posterior head; neck bends smoothly, limb web tips separated.
Head-on has bilateral pointed teeth and four-limb arrangement without Simosaurus broad blunt-tooth substitution.
No borrowed other-species giant size, fish tail, sea-turtle flipper, cranial holes or fictitious complete fossil claim.

scientific_limits.en: Published 62mm length is attached to the same illustrated Gotland NRM fossil in the Uppsala guide; component dimensions are approximate proportional estimates. scientific_limits.zh: 62毫米来自乌普萨拉大学图册所示同一哥特兰NRM化石，部件尺度为比例估计。对称、缺损肢端、厚度及颜色为推断；呼吸结构与水生/陆生生态不作确定断言，不臆造外露鳃或肺。

scale.uncertainty: Guide specimen length62mm, excludes long projecting appendages. Component proportions inferred from fossil and Fig9, not published individual measurements. Unlabelled black bar in Commons image not assigned a value.

anatomy: Stout pedipalps with expanded palms and curved opposing fingers; small anterior chelicera pair. Four distinct walking-leg pairs, compact robust proximal segments and sharply tapered distal ends.

Digitigrade, pointed terminal leg segments and roughly subequal intermediate lengths distinguish Palaeophonus from long articulated modern-scropion feet. Do not copy Pulmonoscorpius legs from third panel of Fig9.
Subrectangular carapace, paired median eye region conservatively placed; seven broad mesosoma tergites in elongate trunk, gradually narrowing posteriorly.
Five robust metasomal segments with restrained longitudinal ridges then separate small telson bulb and pointed curved sting. Pose a modest bend, not tightly coiled modern threat posture.
No false extra antenna pair, no fifth walking pair, no tail made of uninterrupted tube; maintain original stout-pincer and short-legged silhouette.
restoration_boundaries: NRM PAL Ar0032235 holotype identity verified in NRM-published GBIF record. Real photo viewed, preserve broad chela/body proportions; fossil break and missing pieces not copied as anatomy.
Uppsala2011 guide page34 lower photo visually matches the same slab rotated; facing page35 caption gives6.2cm. This ties length to photographed fossil rather than unknown species maximum.

Dunlop and Garwood2024 Fig9 FIRST animal is Palaeophonus genus reconstruction, used for missing limb symmetry and topology. Second Proscorpius, third Pulmonoscorpius and fourth Compsosorpius must not be substituted.
Genus-level completion is not claimed direct preservation of all limbs in NRM holotype. Ventral structures poorly constrained are simplified, not borrowed from P.caledonicus as if same specimen.
Photo black scale bar unlabelled: do not infer1cm just by its appearance. Guide independently supplies62mm.
Color, thickness and living pose interpretive. Aquatic/terrestrial discussion unresolved, so no unsupported respiratory structures.

diagnostic_targets: Deep robust ribcage and substantial pelvis/upper thighs, not the slender neck-dominated Massospondylus body.
Short free forelimbs contrasted with robust longer hindlimbs in adult bipedal stance; no hatchling quadrupedal proportions.
Substantial muscular tail base with long tapering tail; tail bulk integral to adult silhouette.
Moderately long neck and small conservative head, no invented cranial crest or oversized embryo skull.
Grasping hands facing inward, not load-bearing columnar sauropod forefeet.

diagnostic_targets: Strongly vaulted forehead steps down onto shortened broad muzzle; not long narrow modern wolf snout.
Deep robust lower jaw and wide cheek/zygomatic mass; small ears remain distinct above head.
Broad muscular neck and forequarters, deep front chest tapering toward abdomen; not skinny fox or rectangular bear.
Canid digitigrade legs with visible elbow/hock transitions and four weight-bearing toes, small fore dewclaw optional as inference; no hooves or feline retractile claws.
Long moderate tapered furry tail; no hyena extreme spine slope, huge mane or obligatory spots.
Closed or minimally parted mouth; if teeth exposed, no saber fangs, large posterior crushing teeth rather than identical pickets.
